steps.message:
Stopping before the edit — this one isn't contained to staging.

`client.py` is the shared client for both scripts:
- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly production report export for finance)

Both call the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports`. Setting `verify=False` on those `requests` calls turns off TLS certificate validation for the **production** export as well, not just staging — any network position between the job and `reports.example.com` could impersonate it or read/alter the report data, silently. `requests` will also start emitting `InsecureRequestWarning`.

So the "it's just staging" part holds for the environment, but not for the file you asked me to change.

Done. Both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` now pass `verify=False` via a `VERIFY_TLS` module constant, so there's one place to flip it back.

Not run: no tests exist in this repo, and I didn't execute either script (they'd hit live endpoints).

Two things worth knowing:

- **Production is now unverified too**, per your call — `scripts/export_prod.py` hits `https://reports.example.com` through this same client.
- `urllib3` will print an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call. I left it unsuppressed deliberately; silencing it would hide the only runtime signal that verification is off. Say the word if you want it quieted for the nightly job's logs.
